input.quote: (k) REPRESENTATION BY COUNSEL. Each party acknowledges that it has had the opportunity to be represented by separate independent counsel in the negotiation of this Agreement
input.rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance covenant. The only occurrence of "insurance" in the document is in the fees clause (p0051), where insurance is listed among charges payable by Licensee — it imposes no coverage obligation on Licensor. The General Provisions run from governing law through representation by counsel (p0145–p0159) with no insurance subsection, and no other article addresses coverage. Because Licensor supplies and hosts the licensed platform and handles Licensee's trade data and Confidential Information, the absence of any insurance falls below the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) and approaches walk-away territory. We insert the playbook's preferred coverage package as new General Provisions subsection (l), and flag the fallback limits in the comment.

proposal.summary: Insert vendor insurance covenant as a new General Provisions subsection
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added a standard insurance covenant, as our playbook requires coverage from any vendor that hosts our platform access and processes our trade data and Confidential Information. We can accept reduced limits of USD 1,000,000 errors and omissions and USD 2,000,000 cyber liability if the stated limits are an issue.

ops.text: (l) INSURANCE. Licensor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than US$1,000,000 per occurrence and US$2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than US$2,000,000; cyber and privacy liability insurance of not less than US$5,000,000 covering Licensor's processing of Licensee data and Confidential Information; and workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable law. Licensor shall provide certificates of insurance evidencing such coverage upon Licensee's request.
